title: Validate a length-prefixed frame
description: Implement int valid_frame(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len).
prompt:
Implement int valid_frame(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len).
A frame has one payload-length byte N, then N payload bytes, then one checksum byte. The checksum equals the sum of payload bytes modulo 256. Accept exactly N + 2 bytes and reject truncated or trailing data. A zero-length payload is valid with checksum zero.
constraints: buf may be NULL when len is zero.
Never read a byte before checking it is present.

tests.name: Valid payload
Empty payload
Truncated input
Bad checksum
Modulo checksum

rubric: Respect the stated contract and bounds.
Explain integer widths, ownership, and relevant edge cases.
Separate host-test evidence from hardware guarantees.
follow_ups: Which boundary conditions would you test on the target?
What changes if the function is called from an ISR?
hints: Write down the boundary cases before choosing an implementation.
Use explicit integer widths and keep intermediate values in range.
